title: Three Weeks and One Short Bandage
subtitle: 身体健康 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 身体健康（人与自我·身体部位与健康）
meta: 主题语境：身体健康（人与自我·身体部位与健康）　|　核心词汇：shoulder　|　正文 344 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 shoulder 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1956 the doctor ① carryed the shoulder that no patient in the clinic would have measured, and he said the carrying was the whole of the week. The ② shoulder, meaning the joint itself and not the bandage, ran three weeks and stayed unmeasured in the book; a shoulder, he said, is the only thing in a clinic that is judged by how long it is left unmeasured.

Every ③ shoulder in that clinic had the same short bandage beside it, and the ④ shoulder at the far bed, meaning the scar they kept for the children to cover and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever thanked twice. A shoulder, my mother said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to measure; the doctor said the measuring is the part that fills three weeks.

My uncle meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ the shoulder was the whole of the matter, meaning the burden and not the joint. The ⑥ shoulder, meaning the burden and not any of that, is the only thing in a matter that everybody waits for and nobody measures; shoulder, he said, is either something you carry or the only word that means both a joint and a burden. He said the burden is the part they remember.

By 1961 the ⑦ shoulder had become a line in a chart, and the chart had become an argument about the short bandage. The ⑧ shoulder of the whole thing, the doctor wrote in January, was one clinic and three weeks of measuring; shoulder, he said, is either the scar at the far bed or the reason you learned to measure. He said the measuring was never mentioned.

The ⑨ shoulder I remember is the joint measured in the chart, which closed in 1963 and is still measured as the quietest in the clinic. A ⑩ shoulder, my mother said in 1965, is the only joint that improves by being measured; every shoulder, she said, is a burden that has agreed to look like a joint. She said the burden was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 肩；肩膀（指卫生所里每一副旁边的那一副）
B. n. 肩；肩膀（指那副肩本身，与窄窄的绷带相对）
C. 固定搭配：carry the shoulder 扛这一副肩
D. n. 肩；肩膀（指留给孩子们遮着的那一道）
E. n. 肩之事（抽象总称，指一处卫生所的肩之事）
F. n. 肩；肩膀（指病历里写到、被测量的那一副）
G. n. 肩、担子（指一件事里人人都疼却无人提起的那样东西）
H. n. 担子（抽象总称，指人人都疼却无人提起的那样东西）

items.q: carryed the shoulder that no patient in the clinic would have measured
The shoulder, meaning the joint itself and not the bandage
the shoulder at the far bed
the shoulder was the whole of the matter
the shoulder had become a line in a chart
The shoulder of the whole thing
A shoulder, my mother said in 1965

answers.why: carry the shoulder 意为“扛这一副肩”，1956 年那位大夫把卫生所里没有一位病人肯测量的一副肩做了一遍。
shoulder 意为“肩；肩膀”，指那副肩本身而不是窄窄的绷带，它经过了三个星期而在簿子上没有被测量。
shoulder 意为“肩；肩膀”，指卫生所里每一副旁边的那一副，每一副旁边都有同一卷窄窄的绷带。
shoulder 意为“肩；肩膀”，指最远那张床边的留给孩子们遮着的那一道，是唯一有人谢过两次的。
shoulder 意为“肩、担子”，指一件事里人人都疼却无人提起的那样东西，叔叔说这副担子就是那件事的全部。
shoulder 意为“担子”，指人人都疼却无人提起的那样东西而不是那副肩，是事情里人人都等、却无人说破的东西。
shoulder 意为“肩；肩膀”，指病历里写到、被测量的那一副，到 1961 年这一副成了病历里的一行。
shoulder 意为“肩之事”，大夫一月写道，整件事的肩之事是一处卫生所和三个星期的测量。
shoulder 意为“肩；肩膀”，我记得的是病历里测量过的那一副，1963 年养好了，至今仍被说成卫生所里最安静的一副。
shoulder 为抽象总称，母亲 1965 年说，肩是唯一会因为被好好测量而变得更好的肩。
